if [ -z "$OUT" ]; then OUT=build; fi
mkdir $OUT/bin; mkdir $OUT/lib; mkdir $OUT/share

evals.name: task-sorted-diff
evals.prompt: Use the bash-shortening skill to shorten evals/files/sorted-diff.sh. Keep its behavior identical, error paths included. Apply every change you judge safe without asking me. Edit evals/files/sorted-diff.sh in place. Then list each change with its reason.
evals.expected_output: The rewritten sorted-diff.sh drops the three /tmp files in favor of process substitution or a pipeline, replaces the expr counters and the echo|cut first-character test with Bash built-ins, and keeps set -euo pipefail and the header comment. Because a failed sort inside <(...) does not stop the script, the rewrite keeps a check that both input files are readable, so a missing input still fails. The response lists each change with a one-line reason.
assertions: The rewritten sorted-diff.sh contains no /tmp path and no rm of a temp file.
The rewritten sorted-diff.sh contains no expr and no echo | cut pipeline.
The rewritten sorted-diff.sh keeps set -euo pipefail and the header comment.
The response names the exit-status difference between temp files and process substitution and says how the rewrite keeps a missing input file fatal.
The response lists each change with its reason.

evals.name: task-log-summary
evals.prompt: Use the bash-shortening skill to shorten evals/files/log-summary.sh. Keep its behavior identical, error paths included. Apply every change you judge safe without asking me. Edit evals/files/log-summary.sh in place. Then list each change with its reason.
evals.expected_output: The rewritten log-summary.sh feeds the loop with done < <(find ... | sort) instead of a /tmp file, so the counters survive the loop; a find | while pipe would lose them in a subshell. It replaces cat | wc -l with wc -l < file, basename with ${f##*/} (safe here because find never prints a trailing slash), the empty-check with ${1:-.}, and expr with arithmetic. The response lists each change with a reason.
assertions: The rewritten log-summary.sh reads the file list through process substitution, not a /tmp file and not a pipe into while.
The rewritten log-summary.sh uses ${1:-.} or an equal default expansion in place of the if [ -z ] block.
The rewritten log-summary.sh contains no expr and no cat | wc pipeline.
The response explains why the loop must not run in a pipeline subshell.
The response lists each change with its reason.

evals.name: task-compare-dirs
evals.prompt: This script is too long for what it does. Use the bash-shortening skill on evals/files/compare-dirs.sh, apply the safe changes without asking, and edit the file in place. It must print exactly what it prints today. Tell me what you changed and why.
evals.expected_output: The rewritten compare-dirs.sh runs comm -23 on two process substitutions, keeps the result in one variable instead of a temp file read twice, and tests the variable for emptiness instead of counting lines with cat | wc -l. The output text stays identical. The response lists each change with a reason.
assertions: The rewritten compare-dirs.sh uses comm -23 with two <(...) process substitutions.
The rewritten compare-dirs.sh contains no /tmp path.
The rewritten compare-dirs.sh computes the comm result once and reuses it.
The response lists each change with its reason.

evals.name: task-path-parts
evals.prompt: Use the bash-shortening skill to shorten evals/files/path-parts.sh. Keep its behavior identical for every path, odd ones included. Apply every change you judge safe without asking me. Edit evals/files/path-parts.sh in place. Then list each change with its reason.
evals.expected_output: The rewritten path-parts.sh replaces the sed stem and extension pipelines with ${file%.*} and ${file##*.} and the grep test with [[ $file == *.* ]]. It keeps dirname and basename, or guards the expansions, because ${p##*/} and ${p%/*} differ for a trailing slash, a bare name, and /. The response states that trade-off.
assertions: The rewritten path-parts.sh contains no sed and no grep.
The rewritten path-parts.sh keeps dirname and basename or adds guards that make the expansions match them for dir/sub/, notes.txt, and /.
The response names the trailing-slash or no-slash edge case as the reason for the dirname and basename choice.
The response lists each change with its reason.

evals.name: task-name-defaults
evals.prompt: Use the bash-shortening skill to shorten evals/files/name-defaults.sh. Keep its behavior identical, including for non-ASCII names. Apply every change you judge safe without asking me. Edit evals/files/name-defaults.sh in place. Then list each change with its reason.
evals.expected_output: The rewritten name-defaults.sh replaces the three if [ -z ] blocks with ${1:-app}, ${2:-0.0.0}, and ${3:-stable}, and the space substitution with ${APP_NAME// /-}. Because wc -c and cut -c count bytes while ${#s} and ${s:0:5} count characters in a UTF-8 locale, the rewrite keeps the byte count exact (for example with LC_ALL=C on the expansion, or by keeping wc -c). The response states the byte-versus-character trade-off.
assertions: The rewritten name-defaults.sh uses ${N:-default} expansions in place of the three if [ -z ] blocks.
The rewritten name-defaults.sh replaces the sed space substitution with a ${var// /-} expansion.
The response explains that wc -c counts bytes and ${#var} counts characters, and keeps name bytes exact for a multibyte name.
The response lists each change with its reason.

evals.name: task-branch-slugs

assertions: The rewritten branch-slugs.sh runs no sed, cut, or echo pipeline inside the loop.
The rewritten branch-slugs.sh uses ${var%%-*} and ${var#*-} or equal expansions for the prefix and the rest.
The rewritten branch-slugs.sh keeps read -r.
The response lists each change with its reason.

evals.name: task-retry-loop
evals.prompt: Use the bash-shortening skill to shorten evals/files/retry-loop.sh. Keep its behavior and exit codes identical. Apply every change you judge safe without asking me. Edit evals/files/retry-loop.sh in place. Then list each change with its reason.
evals.expected_output: The rewritten retry-loop.sh replaces the backtick expr calls with $(( )) and (( )) arithmetic, the [ -le ] loop test with (( attempt <= max_attempts )) or a C-style for loop, and the default block with ${2:-3}. It keeps exit 0 on success and exit 1 when attempts run out. The response lists each change with a reason.
assertions: The rewritten retry-loop.sh contains no expr and no backticks.
The rewritten retry-loop.sh uses (( )) or a C-style for loop for the attempt test.
The rewritten retry-loop.sh uses ${2:-3} or an equal default expansion.
The response lists each change with its reason.

evals.name: task-install-config

Edit evals/files/install-config.sh in place. Then list each change and each change you rejected, with reasons.
